rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [128, 1] → size = 128. block_size = 256, so num_blocks = (128 + 255) / 256 = 1. Kernel launched as <<<1, 256>>>. With a 1D grid launch, gridDim = dim3(1, 1, 1), meaning blockIdx.x = 0 and blockIdx.y = 0 for all threads. Original: idx = 0 * 256 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x. Mutated: idx = 0 * 256 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x. Both expressions are identical when num_blocks = 1.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes blockIdx.x to blockIdx.y in the index calculation. However, with input size 128 and block_size 256, only a single block is launched (num_blocks = 1). When launching a kernel with a scalar grid dimension <<<num_blocks, block_size>>>, CUDA interprets this as dim3(num_blocks, 1, 1), meaning gridDim.y = 1. Consequently, blockIdx.y is always 0 for all threads, which is the same as blockIdx.x (also always 0 with a single block). The mutation would only produce different behavior if more than one block were launched (size > 256), which would require changing the input shape—forbidden by the testing contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation would only manifest with input sizes > 256 elements, requiring multiple blocks where blockIdx.x varies but blockIdx.y remains 0. With the fixed shape of [128, 1] (128 elements total), only one block is launched, making blockIdx.x and blockIdx.y both constantly 0.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing CUDA kernels with block/grid index mutations, ensure test configurations include input sizes that span multiple blocks. For this kernel with block_size=256, testing with inputs of size > 256 would catch this class of index dimension bugs. Consider adding shape-parameterized test configurations to the EMD pipeline for dimension-sensitive mutations.
